primary_claim: Activation Oracles (LLMs trained to answer arbitrary natural-language questions about LLM activations) achieve state-of-the-art performance on 3 of 4 downstream auditing tasks (secret elicitation and emergent-misalignment detection), despite never being trained on activations from the fine-tuned target models, and performance scales predictably with training data quantity and diversity.

effect.metric: auditing task performance vs prior methods
effect.value: AOs match or exceed the best prior method on 3/4 auditing tasks; beat all baseline methods on 2/3 secret-keeping evals (3/3 among white-box methods)

contradicts_or_qualifies: the one task where AOs are not the best or tied-for-best method was Secret Side Constraint, a setting where black-box prompting techniques can induce the target model to reveal its secret knowledge
stated_future_work: excited about hybrid methods, such as applying AOs to interpret SAE error terms
limitations_stated: AOs are not exhaustive; they will not tell you everything about an activation, including questions we don't know to ask
AOs might be too expressive, risking that explanations reflect the AO's own understanding rather than the target LLM's, including confabulation
AOs are expensive at inference time, requiring multiple forward passes to answer a single question
AOs are a fundamentally non-mechanistic technique, unsuited to questions about how meaning is encoded or how computations process activations
quote: We find that our AOs achieve state-of-the-art performance on 3 out of 4 of these auditing tasks.
